facts.statement: Rhizodus belonged to the Rhizodontida, one of the earliest-diverging tetrapodomorph clades.
facts.quote: It belonged to Rhizodontida, one of the earliest-diverging tetrapodomorph clades

facts.statement: The type species Rhizodus hibberti was discovered in the Viséan stage of the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: The species Rhizodus serpukhovensis was discovered in the Serpukhovian of Russia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Rhizodus have also been found in North America.

facts.statement: The partial lower jaw found in Russia was formally described as the new species R. serpukhovensis in 2022.

facts.statement: R. hibberti measured between 5.14 and 5.63 meters long and weighed between 1 and 1.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: with R. hibberti measuring 5.14 - 5.63 m long and weighing 1 - 1.5 MT

facts.statement: Both valid species of Rhizodus lived during the Early Carboniferous epoch.

facts.statement: Rhizodus lived from the Tournaisian to the Gzhelian, between 358.86 and 298.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tournaisian to Gzhelian (358.86 to 298.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Rhizodus is classified in the class Sarcopterygii.
Rhizodus was scientifically described by Owen in 1840.
facts.quote: Este género marino fue descrito científicamente por Owen en 1840

facts.statement: Rhizodus gracilis is a species of Rhizodus described by M'Coy in 1848.
Rhizodus hibberti is a species of Rhizodus described by Agassiz in 1843.
Rhizodus ornatus is a species of Rhizodus described by Traquair in 1836.
A 2020 study suggested dividing rhizodont humeri into four morphogroups to better identify Rhizodus.
